sections.h2: Who do I call about a Floyd County tax bill?
sections.html:
Two do. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) decides what a parcel is worth. The sheriff's tax division handles the bill itself. Neither one chooses the rate applied to that value.

The PVA's own site says the office appraises real and personal property at fair market value and stays out of rate setting, tax calculation and collection. Its counter is at 149 S. Central Ave., Room 5, in Prestonsburg, and the phone is (606) 886-9622. The sheriff keeps the tax division in the same building, takes mail at P.O. Box 152, and answers tax calls at (606) 886-8965 from 8:00 to 4:00 on weekdays.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Floyd County's housing market?
sections.html:
Floyd County lies in the Eastern Kentucky coalfield. It has 393 square miles of land and borders Johnson, Martin, Pike, Knott and Magoffin counties. Lawmakers created it at the end of 1799 as the state's 40th county, and the law took effect on June 1, 1800. The first courthouse burned in April 1808, which is why the earliest surviving government records start after that year.

Coal explains most of the housing map. Eastern Kentucky's first commercial coal mine opened in 1900 at Betsy Layne, and coal camps such as Wheelwright, Wayland, Garrett, Emma and Bypro grew up around the mines. Floyd County topped 53,000 people in 1950 and has lost residents in almost every census since; the 2020 count was 35,942. By 2016 the county still had 23 working mines producing roughly 640,000 tons.

Prestonsburg is the seat, and Allen, Martin, Wayland and Wheelwright are the other cities. Census-designated places include Auxier, Betsy Layne, Dwale, Maytown and McDowell. Just 21.8 percent of the 2020 population counted as urban, so many sellers own hillside or hollow land instead of a town lot. The Floyd County School District runs the public schools.

sections.h2: How do Floyd County's housing figures read?
sections.html:
They describe a low-priced, owner-heavy market with little new construction.

  • Estimated 2025 population: 34,401, down 4.3 percent since 2020.
  • Typical value of a house its owner lives in (2020 to 2024 survey period): $98,700.
  • Owner-occupied share: 72.2 percent, across 14,700 households that average 2.34 people.
  • Housing units: 17,753 in 2025, with 13.8 percent sitting empty when the 2020 census was taken.
  • Median gross rent: $672. Median household income: $41,279. People in poverty: 27.7 percent.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 2.

Just 43.5 percent of adults are in the labor force, and 22.3 percent of residents younger than 65 report a disability. Health care brought in about $355 million in 2022, more than any other sector listed by the Census Bureau for the county. On a house worth about $98,700, a few thousand dollars of back tax eats a visible slice of the price, so paying it off early counts for more here than in a county with pricier homes.

sections.h2: When does Floyd County expect payment, and what happens if I am late?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 sets the calendar, and it favors early payers. Pay the whole bill by November 1 and 2 percent comes off. After that the printed amount applies until December 31. January costs an extra 5 percent, and anything later costs 10 percent.

The sheriff's site announced that 2026 bills were payable from October 1 and added an online payment link. If a lender escrows your taxes, check that the servicer actually received the bill.

On April 15 the sheriff hands every open bill over to the county clerk. A lien is recorded, and interest of 1 percent accrues monthly. The clerk adds a 10 percent commission, and once the county attorney has sent a notice, a 20 percent attorney commission follows. A clerk's tax sale follows within roughly three to four and a half months.

sections.h2: How can a Floyd County owner contest a value?
sections.html:
Go to the PVA first. Kentucky requires a conference there before an appeal can be filed, and the PVA must walk you through the valuation method.

  • The roll is posted for public viewing over 13 days that start in early May.
  • The written appeal goes to the county clerk, and the cutoff is the end of the first business day after viewing closes.
  • A local review board hears cases roughly four to five weeks after viewing ends, so spend the wait collecting photos, repair quotes and nearby sale prices.
  • Missing the hearing forfeits the later step to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Hired representatives must come from a short list of professions in KRS 133.120 and carry your written permission.

sections.h2: Does a Floyd County homeowner qualify for the homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Age 65 and up, or total disability, opens the door to a $49,100 reduction in assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 years. The Floyd County PVA site says nobody receives an exemption without filing a formal application, and that the disability route is meant for people who are 100 percent disabled.

With a median-priced Floyd County house at $98,700, the taxable figure becomes $49,600. To prove age, bring a birth certificate, license or passport. Someone applying on disability grounds needs proof of a total-disability classification and has to reapply annually. Veterans with a service-connected disability and people whose disability is permanent under Social Security rules are spared the yearly paperwork.

sections.h2: How should I handle unpaid taxes when selling a Floyd County house?
sections.html:
Pay them off, or have the closing agent do it. KRS 134.015 keeps a delinquency lien on the parcel whoever holds title, so the buyer's title company will find it.

  • Call the sheriff's tax division at (606) 886-8965 for the exact payoff.
  • Pay before April 15 if you can, because the clerk and attorney commissions only begin after the transfer.
  • Put the current year's bill in the sale contract. The state treats the tax as owed by the person who held the property on January 1.
  • If repairs and arrears are both piling up, a direct buyer that purchases as-is can fold both into one closing.

The county clerk can explain how to record the deed. Afterward, send the PVA the new owner's name and mailing address.

faqs.q: Where do Floyd County residents pay their property tax?
faqs.a: At the Floyd County Sheriff's tax division, 149 S Central Ave. in Prestonsburg, by mail to P.O. Box 152, or online from the sheriff's home page. The tax division's number is (606) 886-8965.

faqs.q: Does the Floyd County PVA set my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The PVA's website says the office does not determine rates, calculate taxes or collect them. It values property and processes exemption applications at (606) 886-9622.

faqs.q: When does Floyd County's 2 percent discount end?
faqs.a: On November 1. From November 2 through December 31 the bill is due without a discount, and penalties start in January.

faqs.q: How large is the homestead exemption for a Floyd County home?
faqs.a: The reduction is $49,100 for both 2025 and 2026. Eligible owners are seniors and the totally disabled, and the paperwork goes to the Floyd County PVA.

faqs.q: Can a Floyd County house sell while tax is still owed?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the balance is settled by the closing table. Request a payoff from the sheriff first, since an open bill leaves the lien on the parcel.
